scientific_question: Can detector-specific target-normal score deformation identify the direction and magnitude of a safe operating-point threshold correction without using target anomaly labels?

frozen_background.frozen_interpretation: PB6 QM's positive delta_BA is operating-point rebalancing, not representation/ranking capability improvement. FNR_after = 14/15 on 117/117 entities. QM benefit requires FNR_before >= 0.9133. EfficientAD QM oracle headroom = 0/39 (correct abstention); BC_RANK O2/O3 headroom ~ 2/39; general score-threshold O4 headroom = 11/39. QM mean delta_AUROC = -0.0772; 33/33 QM benefit rows from already-failed operating points.

DEPLOYABLE.definition: usable by any deployable candidate / feature / actuator; must never depend on target anomaly labels, anomaly scores, or any oracle outcome

inputs.condition_metadata: acquisition condition metadata (OPTIONAL; no PB7 candidate may depend on the condition label directly)

ORACLE_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY.definition: usable ONLY for oracle diagnostic targets (O1/O2/O3) and diagnostic metrics; never a deployment input; never used to fit, select, or calibrate any deployable candidate

firewall.mechanism: code-level Firewall in pb7_p0_common.py: every score read is recorded with role; deployable computation must call assert_deployable_clean() which raises FIREWALL_VIOLATION if any anomaly (oracle-only) file was read on that path

data_roles.leakage_rule: if any deployable candidate directly or indirectly uses target-bad / anomaly information, it is immediately marked LEAKAGE_INVALID and excluded from formal comparison

grid.generation: all unique values of the pooled target scores (target-normal U anomaly) PLUS the source threshold tau_source, sorted ascending
grid.endpoint_handling: grid includes min and max pooled scores; both endpoints are valid candidates (BA at extremes is typically 0.5); no clipping, no padding
grid.exactness: BA/FPR/FNR are step functions of tau, so scanning the unique pooled scores is exact for the decision boundary

estimands.tie_break: among thresholds achieving the target optimum, choose the one closest to tau_source; further tie -> smaller tau

O1_ORACLE_BA_OPTIMAL_THRESHOLD.definition: tau*_BA = argmax over the frozen grid of BA(score > tau); tie-break closest to tau_source, further tie smaller tau

O2_ORACLE_SAFE_CONSTRAINED_THRESHOLD.definition: tau*_SAFE = argmax over the frozen grid of BA subject to FNR(tau) - FNR(tau_source) <= +0.02 (delta_fnr <= +0.02); tie-break closest to tau_source, further tie smaller tau
O2_ORACLE_SAFE_CONSTRAINED_THRESHOLD.feasibility: tau_source is always feasible (delta_fnr = 0), so the feasible set is never empty

O3_ORACLE_CORRECTABILITY_LABEL.definition: CORRECTABLE_SAFE = 1 iff delta_ba >= +0.02 AND delta_fpr <= -0.05 AND delta_fnr <= +0.02 relative to the source operating point (the frozen benefit definition), evaluated at tau*_SAFE; otherwise 0

H1_THRESHOLD_HEADROOM_EXISTS.claim: at least one detector has a non-trivial fraction of units with CORRECTABLE_SAFE = 1
H1_THRESHOLD_HEADROOM_EXISTS.minimum_continuation: >= 20% of units OR >= 8 units (at least one satisfied)

H2_DIRECTION_IDENTIFIABILITY.claim: normal-only deformation can predict sign(tau*_SAFE - tau_source) significantly better than a trivial baseline

H3_MAGNITUDE_IDENTIFIABILITY.claim: normal-only deformation has a stable monotonic / regression relation with delta_tau*_SAFE

H4_DETECTOR_DEPENDENCE.claim: different detectors show substantial differences in correctability prevalence, delta_tau* distribution, and the deformation -> threshold relationship

H5_FEW_NORMAL_STABILITY.claim: the above information is preserved with sufficient stability at K=8 target-normal support

H6_SAFE_DEPLOYABLE_ACTUATOR_EXISTS.claim: at least one pre-registered simple normal-only threshold rule achieves actual benefit under strict held-out evaluation

k_support.tri_detector_extension: PB3 seed manifest covers the 2 reference detectors; the third detector (efficientad) uses the same frozen seed identity via the PB6 D8 tri_k8_indices rule

forbidden: select features by test anomaly outcome
add new rules ad hoc from detector results
treat oracle thresholds as deployable methods
use target anomaly labels to construct any deployable predictor
use target anomaly score distribution as a deployable input
redefine candidate actuators after seeing held-out results
describe AUROC-invariant threshold correction as detection capability improvement
leakage_rule: if any deployable candidate directly or indirectly uses target-bad / anomaly information, it is immediately marked LEAKAGE_INVALID and excluded from formal comparison

conditions: oracle threshold semantics are unique (grid/tie-break/endpoints frozen)
